ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$ and intersects $BC$ at $D$. If $BC=7\text{cm}$ and $BD=4\text{cm}$, what is the distance from point $D$ to $AB$ in $\text{cm}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw DH $\perp$ AB at point H, \\
$\because$ BC = 7cm, BD = 4cm, \\
$\therefore$ CD = 7 - 4 = 3cm, \\
Also, $\because$ AD is the bisector of $\angle BAC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, and DH $\perp$ AB, \\
$\therefore$ DH = CD = 3cm, \\
$\therefore$ the distance from point D to AB is \boxed{3} cm.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached diagram shows triangle ABC with AC drawn vertically on the left, CB drawn horizontally along the bottom, B to the right, and A above C. Point D lies on segment CB between C and B, and segment AD is drawn from A to D, matching the statement that AD bisects angle BAC. The problem text states that ∠C = 90°. Reasoning: Since BC = 7 cm and BD = 4 cm, we get CD = BC - BD = 7 - 4 = 3 cm. Draw DH perpendicular to AB, so DH is the distance from D to AB. Because D lies on the angle bisector AD of angle BAC, D is equidistant from the two sides of the angle, AB and AC. The perpendicular distance from D to AC is CD, since AC is perpendicular to BC and D lies on BC. Thus the distance from D to AB equals CD = 3 cm.
